features.name: Lake Enner
features.notes: The hoarder. Does not freeze, does not ripple, warm at the bottom.

features.name: Lake Sere
features.notes: Salt. Held by the Tarsk.

features.name: the Brine Mere
features.notes: Shallow brine and salt flats; the Sallowmen's pans ring it.

features.name: the Carrow Water
features.notes: The stream in Carrow itself, split from its lower course so that a god who has seen only the valley is not shown the rest.

features.name: the Corr
features.notes: The same water as the Wend above and the Sarn below.

features.name: the Enn
features.notes: Ends in Lake Enner over a fall at the north rim.

features.name: the Maund
features.notes: Rises from warm springs under the south rim. No water is seen to leave the lake.

features.name: the Tarrow
features.notes: Runs west into Lake Sere.

features.name: Vorn
features.notes: Dry: no spring, no stream, no snow-melt runnel on it.

features.name: the Howe
features.notes: A low grassed hill, 150 feet. Too small for the paint. A barrow of the Old Maund kings.

features.name: the Carrow Pass
features.notes: Shut by snow from the eleventh month to the fourth. Sallow side beyond.

features.name: the High Stair
features.notes: Leads north over the Skarn and off the sheet. Open ten weeks a year.

features.name: the Upper Hamlet
features.notes: Nine houses. The stone-wife lives here. The Carrowfolk call it Tophouses.

features.name: Flockmeet
features.notes: The lowest and largest hamlet, about 160 people. The autumn gathering is held on its green.

features.name: Brinehall
features.notes: The Sallowmen's town on the north shore of the Brine Mere.

features.name: Middle Stair
features.notes: The winter-count stone stands here.

features.name: Eelholm
features.notes: The Long Roof.

features.name: Sarnmouth
features.notes: Chief of the Three Havens.

features.name: Postlanding
features.notes: The flood post and the meeting house.

features.name: Piers
features.notes: The old bridge.

features.name: Whitepans
features.notes: Free salt town.

features.name: Serewell
features.notes: The Tarsk wintering ground and salt market. Tents and a few timber stores.

features.name: Ennerhold
features.notes: The city of Ennermere, in the Gap.

features.name: Fallwater
features.notes: Where the Enn falls to the lake.

features.name: Hithe-under-Hill
features.notes: East shore.

features.name: Under-Hithe
features.notes: A shore hamlet of about thirty people with no house names.

features.name: Gullet
features.notes: About 110 people under a cracked slope.

features.name: the Tasteless Field
features.notes: Two miles of overdrawn ground where Old Maund's first city stood.

features.name: Farhall
features.notes: The westernmost Edgefolk steading.

features.name: the Old Men
features.notes: Three slab cairns on the Carrow Pass, each of slabs no valley team could move. High Road markers. About 6,000 years old.

features.name: the Walled Fold
features.notes: A sheepfold with its gate walled shut, above the Upper Hamlet. The Hollin dead of the sickness winter lie in it under turf.

features.name: the Shut House
features.notes: A sealed door in an outcrop on Windlow Moor, on the High Road. An Abider lives behind it.

features.name: the Hask steadings
features.notes: Four dead steadings and a burial ground of 212.

features.name: the Sighting Stones
features.notes: Two pairs of stones a thousand years apart in age, each pair once framing the star.

features.name: the Leaf Halls
features.notes: Buried halls with carved walls, leaf and trunk. The way in is a shaft in a sheepwalk.

features.name: the Soft House
features.notes: The temple of Enna, the god that went up. Its stones have gone soft at the edges.

features.name: the Ringing Stair
features.notes: A well-shaft and stair through four layers of ruin to the Glass.

features.name: the Sworn Door
features.notes: A door in the rock facing away from the lake, an oath cut round its frame in Abider script.

features.name: the Law Stones
features.notes: A field of fallen law stelae of the Corr kingdoms and a store of clay tablets no one can read.

features.name: the Old Bins
features.notes: Footings and one corner of an Old Maund granary. Barley grows inside.

features.name: the Three Bins
features.notes: Three Old Maund granaries still roofed, sealed and empty.

features.name: the Dry Loft
features.notes: A sealed hill store of Old Maund. Jars of seed barley, still alive.

features.name: the Ribs
features.notes: Seven long grassed ridges side by side that farmers plough around. Bones.

features.name: the Drowned Road
features.notes: Squared stones running into the water toward the south-west.

features.name: the Singing Door
features.notes: Under four feet of water at low summer level. A door that opens to a sung phrase.

features.name: the Debt Door
features.notes: A sealed door in a hillside, shut 380 years ago to keep a pledge.

features.name: Highbank
features.notes: Green banks of an older town on a hilltop.

features.name: the Edge Mounds
features.notes: A line of nine grassed mounds.

features.name: the King Mounds
features.notes: Forty mounds of the mound-builders.

features.name: the Door of Vorn
features.notes: The Abiders' door. It is not sealed. It is not easy to see.

features.name: Marrowden
features.notes: Lair of the old bear the Edgefolk call the Marrow-Eater.

features.name: the Halls of Vorn
features.notes: About 600 Abiders. The Count is cut on the walls of the lowest hall.

features.name: the hall behind the Shut House
features.notes: One Abider, Ninth-of-the-Door.

features.name: the Sunk Hall
features.notes: Flooded to the knee. Empty since the drowning of Halmer.

features.name: the hall behind the Debt Door
features.notes: Holds the pledge of the Vane and Orrel houses: a bronze cauldron of split tallies.

features.name: the Leaf Halls
features.notes: Five halls in a line. High Ennermere's, 900 years old. Anyone who spends a night inside comes out missing one small particular thing.

features.name: the hall behind the Sworn Door
features.notes: Empty. A stone bench facing the wall away from the lake.

features.name: the Dry Loft
features.notes: Forty sealed jars; nine hold live seed.

features.name: the Glass
features.notes: Blue-grey glass that rings when struck, under everything in the bowl. Reached only by the Ringing Stair.

features.name: the foot of the Ringing Stair
